title: Clip 2:
length: about 4 min 30 s at full script
headline: Imagine losing everything one morning. From detention, the voice that answers is AIJ’s.
story: This is Clip 2 of the client’s final gala script. It opens with “Imagine this”: a life built over decades, gone in one morning. From detention, the call is answered by the AIJ hotline in English, Spanish and Creole.

Then the proof: Sui on the only detention hotline in Florida, Robert, Paul on Alligator Alcatraz, Haitian neighbours, Dreamers and A.D. reunited with his son, survivors, and children in court. It ends on “Not someday. Now.” Warm, not angry. It builds from loss to hope.
do: Cut to the client-final script doc, line by line. Re-read it before each pass: Andrés edits it in place.
Put a real picture on frame 1, with <q>Imagine this.</q>
Record a temp VO for V1 so the timing is real.
Keep the warm section warm. The music builds to the crescendo the client asked for.
Mark every missing visual (animation, Little Haiti, Lucha) with a clear placeholder card.
dont: Never show or name a client. A.D. is “A.D.” only. No operator names.

Don’t use Paul’s “bad cancer” / Florida beta-test lines (C9279 08:37–09:02), insulin/box/mosquito detail (10:13–12:27), 287(g) (15:42–19:27, 28:21–31:07), or “ICE isn’t following their own rules” (23:30).

voice.quote: Imagine this: For decades, you built a life here in the United States, far from the danger that forced you to flee.

rows.music: Music starts soft. It builds through the list.

rows.visual: Warm ordinary shots: work, a neighbour, a father and daughter at a kitchen table, Miami light. Pace picks up as the list grows. B-roll TBD on scrub.

voice.quote: You work hard to support your family. You contribute to your neighborhood, schools, friends, and religious communities. You have a business. You create economic opportunities for others. You pay taxes. You live honestly and follow the law. Importantly, you follow the immigration rules and processes. Your children were born in the United States and you call the U.S. your home.

rows.music: Build to a crescendo with the list.

rows.visual: Last warm shot, then black for under 1 second (the client’s dramatic pause).

voice.quote: Then one morning … it is all gone. You are detained on your way to work.

voice.src: A.D. audio file. Client script text; times not checked.

Over the years, they assisted my family with kindness and compassion. Our lives improved in countless ways, thanks to their dedication. I hope they can continue this vital work for others who face the same struggle I did.
voice.src: Client script, Clip 2. Client audio not delivered yet.

decisions.b: This page follows the client’s final script (5 Oct): Clip 2 is a narrated film with many voices, and the 10 Sep note on this item ties it to Clip 2. The other option is a short Paul-only film (“Fearless”, ending on “hope is not passive”). Confirm.
The 21 Sep call agreed AI voices for the first cut. AIJ asked for human voices on other scripts. Confirm the V1 temp voice and who records the final.
The client script opens on a black screen. House rule is a real picture on frame 1. This page opens on picture. Keep or switch?
At full script this runs about 4½ minutes. The client said past gala videos tired the room. Cut V1 to the full script and flag the length, or trim first?
The intern’s animation, the Lucha client’s audio and Little Haiti shots are not delivered. Who chases AIJ?

client_note: Why this matters: this is the longest gala film and the one with the most client voices. It must stay warm and calm, never angry, even when the story is detention.
